explain.say: In 476 a Germanic general, Odoacer, removed a teenage emperor, Romulus Augustulus, and sent the imperial regalia to Constantinople. No new Western emperor followed. In the 1700s Edward Gibbon blamed what he called the triumph of barbarism and religion. Historians have offered hundreds of causes since. Look at five on the board.

explain.say: First, frontier pressure. In 376 Goths fleeing the Huns crossed the Danube; in 378 they killed Emperor Valens at Adrianople. In 410 Alaric's Goths sacked Rome itself, the first time in 800 years. Why would hungry refugees and a weak government be a dangerous mix?

explain.say: Now the money. Look at the map: the Vandals crossed the Rhine around 406, moved through Gaul and Spain, and in 439 took Carthage, the rich grain and tax land of Africa. Without that tax, the West could not pay its armies. Which matters more for an empire, battles or taxes?

The East, ruled from Constantinople, was richer and survived for nearly a thousand years. Newer research adds plagues and a cooling climate, as in Kyle Harper's The Fate of Rome, 2017. Can you see how several causes feed one another?

explain.say: So, did Rome fall? See the debate. Peter Brown described a lively late antiquity of change, not decline. Bryan Ward-Perkins pointed to vanishing pottery, coins and roof tiles: daily life got poorer. Fantastic work. Exam tip: answer fall or transformation questions by region and by class of people.

faq.q: When did the Western Roman Empire fall?
faq.a: Traditionally in 476, when Odoacer deposed Romulus Augustulus. But it was a long process over the fifth century, and the Eastern Roman Empire lasted until 1453.

faq.q: Why did the Western Roman Empire fall?
faq.a: Historians point to several linked causes: pressure from Goths, Huns and others; civil wars; the loss of tax-rich provinces like Africa; a split from the wealthier East; and perhaps plague and climate change.
asks: What caused the fall of Rome?
What were the Goths and Huns doing?

faq.a: In The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire, 1776 to 1789, Gibbon blamed internal decay, including lost civic virtue, and famously called the outcome the triumph of barbarism and religion.

Peter Brown's idea of late antiquity stresses transformation and continuity, while Bryan Ward-Perkins argues the evidence shows a real collapse in living standards. Many historians now accept both, depending on region and class.

faq.q: What role did disease and climate play?
faq.a: Kyle Harper argues that pandemics, such as the Antonine plague from 165 and the Plague of Justinian from 541, and a cooling climate weakened Rome's population and economy. Other historians think he gives these too much weight.
